description:
Add terminal compaction and the merge protocol so exchange branches land back on main.

=== What to build ===
1. Compactor subagent shape (§2.7). Stub is acceptable per §12 — it can produce a trivial summary (e.g. 'exchange <id>: <terminal response text>') written to .agent/compactions/<seq>.md, with no mark_for_deletion calls for v0.2. What matters is the DISPATCH shape exists.
2. Compactor tool surface: write_summary(content), mark_for_deletion(path). Deletion-only write discipline (§2.7) — no general filesystem writes from the compactor. For v0.2, mark_for_deletion can be unimplemented (no-op) as long as the tool is callable without crash.
3. At exchange-done, the harness dispatches the compactor off the exchange branch tip. Compactor runs on its own branch, writes the summary, merges back into the exchange branch. (v0.2 invocation is permitted here — §2.7 defines the compactor as a subagent.)
4. Merge protocol (§2.6): exchange branch rebases onto main's current tip, --no-ff merges into main. Conflict path is a hard error marked 'conflicted' — v0.2 doesn't need graceful handling beyond a clear message.
5. Cleanup: worktree removed on merge; branch ref retained for the retention window (§2.3, §2.9).

=== Out of scope ===
- Intermediate compaction (§2.7 'intermediate' trigger) — v0.2 is terminal-only.
- Compactor quality improvements — literal stub is fine.
- workflow.yaml-driven compaction triggers (v0.6).
- Rich conflict recovery (mark conflicted and bail).

=== Dependencies ===
- Task A (exchange branch + step on branch).

=== Testing ===
- Unit: compactor dispatch + merge-back flow with injected git/adapter stubs.
- Integration: lernie new → lernie prompt against mock → assert main's HEAD is a merge commit whose second parent is the exchange branch tip; exchange's compacted tree (summary file) is reachable via the merge.
- tarpaulin --fail-under 100 green.
title: Terminal compaction stub + no-ff merge back
